title: The "White Rock" of Shiroishi City
description: Shiroishi City in southern Miyagi is renowned for its reconstructed castle, samurai history, special 'umen' noodles, and the enchanting Zao Fox Village. While exploring attractions and savoring local cuisine are popular activities, researching the origins of the place names offers valuable insights into the history and thoughts of past pioneers. Shiroishi (白石) translates to 'White Rock,' and this rock still exists in a small chained-off enclosure. Located just a 5-minute walk from City Hall or a 10-minute walk from Shiroishi Castle, the rock is accompanied by a pine tree and a historical marker. The 'white' rock is actually ash gray, having weathered the elements for centuries. Standing at 0.47 meters tall and 1.05 meters in diameter, it is considered a resting place for a matchmaking deity. The city is linked to a larger white rock in Neno-Shiroishi, located about 55km away, where prayers for good marriages are said to be fulfilled.

title: Sendai's Flagship Street Food: Hyotan
description: Without a doubt, one of Sendai's must-try street foods is 'hyotan-age'. This delightful snack consists of deep-fried fish balls skewered on a stick, offering a crispy exterior and a soft interior. Served with a swirl of optional ketchup, it resembles an American corndog in texture. You can find hyotan-age at Sendai Station near the tourism information center or at the original Abe Kamaboko shop at the end of the CLIS Road shopping arcade. For just ¥250, this portable snack is perfect for a break during shopping. And if you find the word 'あたり' on your stick, you are a 'winner'!

title: Nakiryu Ramen
description: Nakiryu Ramen (創作麺工房 鳴龍) is a Michelin-starred ramen restaurant located in Tokyo's Otsuka district. Opened in 2012, it quickly became one of Tokyo's best ramen shops, earning its Michelin star in 2017. Nakiryu offers a variety of ramen options, including shoyu, shio, and their signature tantanmen, known for its creamy, spicy broth and handmade ultra-thin noodles. The basic tantanmen starts at ¥900, with spicier and sourer variations available. Open from 11 am to 3:30 pm, closed on Tuesdays, Nakiryu is just a 6-minute walk from Otsuka Station. Don't miss the chance to experience this culinary gem!

title: Youmeiji Temple, Tsuwano
description: Youmeiji Temple (永明寺) is a thatch-roofed temple located 15 minutes from Tsuwano Station and 10 minutes from the old town center. I visited in early summer and felt a refreshing breeze from the tall trees and thick forest after climbing the stairs to the temple. The entrance features a tall gate that once marked the boundary between the merchant town and samurai residences. The temple is quiet, allowing weary travelers to relax. Behind the temple is a small but beautiful garden. Built in 1420 by the Yoshimi clan, it served as the family temple for domain lords until the Meiji Restoration. The graveyard in front includes the resting place of Ogai Mori, a prominent Meiji period writer. A unique hollow fish sculpture serves as a silent alarm for the priests, adding to the temple's serene atmosphere. This is a place worth visiting.

title: Gyorai Ramen
description: Gyorai Ramen (本枯中華そば 魚雷) is a unique ramen shop located in Bunkyo, Tokyo, that opened in 2010. Its standout feature is the use of coffee siphons for soup preparation, which maximizes the smoky flavor from dried bonito. The ramen is served in a 'deconstructed' style, allowing customers to choose their toppings and customize their dish. The basic ramen starts at ¥730, with options for deluxe (¥930) and grilled (¥1,030) versions, each offering a variety of toppings. The soup is made from Aomori jidori chicken, Akaniwatori chicken from Kagoshima, and pork, blended with kombu and various fish flavors. With its innovative cooking method and high-quality ingredients, Gyorai Ramen is a must-visit for ramen lovers.

title: Sunny Hills at Minami
description: Located in the glitzy neighborhood of Omotesando, Sunny Hills (微熱山丘) is a pineapple cake shop housed in a stunning wooden structure designed by renowned architect Kengo Kuma, completed in 2013. This architectural marvel utilizes over 5000 meters of timber and traditional woodcrafting techniques without any nails. Visitors can freely explore the three-story building and enjoy a complimentary pineapple cake, 'Sunny Delights,' along with tea on the second floor, embracing Taiwanese hospitality. It's a perfect spot to unwind away from the bustling Tokyo coffee shops, offering a unique experience in a serene atmosphere.

title: The 1300th Anniversary of Koma
description: In 2016, Koma in Hidaka City, Saitama, celebrates its 1300th anniversary. The name Koma (高麗) is also associated with Goguryeo, an ancient kingdom. The Nihon Shoki records the arrival of Jakko, an envoy from Goguryeo, in Japan. In 716 A.D., Jakko gathered 1,799 Goguryeo refugees and settled them in the Musashino Plain. After his death, the Koma Shrine was built in his memory. Exciting events are planned for May 21-22, 2016, including a memorial concert and the Rainbow Parade, where participants will wear colorful Korean-style clothing, commemorating the arrival of the refugees. A giant pot of Koma Nabe will be served at the end of the parade.

title: Matsumoto Kiyoshi
description: Japan is renowned not only for its high-tech gadgets but also for its excellent cosmetic brands and quality medicines. In Tokyo, you can find numerous drugstores, with Matsumoto Kiyoshi being the largest chain. It offers a wide range of both Japanese and international cosmetics and medicines, making it a perfect shopping destination for beauty-conscious customers. Brands like Shiseido, Kose, and Maybelline are available, along with testers for customers to try before they buy. Additionally, Matsumoto Kiyoshi stocks various products, including food, pet supplies, and toiletries. The store is easily recognizable by its vibrant blue and yellow signage, featuring the kanji for 'medicine' (薬) prominently displayed. Shopping at Matsumoto Kiyoshi promises to be a delightful experience.

title: Kameki Sushi
description: Kameki Sushi (亀喜寿司) is celebrated as one of Japan's top sushi restaurants, frequented by the elite when they travel north of Tokyo. It is featured on the local government's 'Sushi Road' for serving fresh fish from the Shiogama fish markets. With over 80 years of history, Kameki Sushi has grown alongside the success of Shiogama's fishing industry. The menu offers a wide variety of options, including set menus (from ¥5,200), chirashi, nigiri, maki, and sashimi. A highlight is the egg cake with surimi (¥300) from their unique dessert menu. Seasonal specialties abound, showcasing the rich marine life off the East Japan coastline. A visit to Kameki Sushi is a must for sushi enthusiasts traveling through Miyagi Prefecture.

title: 川越「菓子屋横丁」
description: Kawagoe's 'Kashiya Yokocho' began in the early Meiji era, offering sweets loved by the people of Edo. After the Great Kanto Earthquake, it developed as a substitute for Tokyo's confectionery wholesalers, and now features over 20 shops where visitors can enjoy nostalgic flavors. The unique vibrancy of the artisans and the sweet aromas create a delightful atmosphere for strolling and snacking. The close-knit community adds warmth to the experience. Every April, the Kashiya Yokocho Festival is held, showcasing traditional performances. Kawagoe City is also set to host the golf venue for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, with efforts to accommodate foreign tourists.

title: Dagashi
description: Dagashi-ya (駄菓子屋) is a nostalgic shop where children flock after school to buy colorful, inexpensive snacks and toys. The vibrant packaging of treats like bubble gum and curry snacks excites the senses, while prices remain under 200 yen. In addition to snacks, these shops offer commemorative stamps and old bills, making each visit a delightful experience. Collecting these stamps provides a unique glimpse into Japanese art and culture, making Dagashi-ya a must-visit for anyone interested in the charm of childhood and Japanese heritage.

title: ブリジストンゴルフプラザ託麻、熊本 [Closed]
description: Bridgestone Golf Plaza Takuma was an ideal place for golf beginners to receive lessons. For 2100 yen, you could take two one-hour lessons, where instructors provided careful guidance from the basics. The coaches were friendly and offered personalized advice to help improve swings and posture. Group lessons were also available, creating a motivating environment for students. It was a wonderful place to enjoy golf, but unfortunately, it is now permanently closed.

title: My You Bus
description: Kochi City has many charms, but pleasant driving is not one of them. Luckily, the My Yu (MY遊) bus covers great sites around the city, like Katsurahama and Mt. Godaisan, which are otherwise hard to access. With a My Yu bus pass, you get discounted admission to attractions along the route and unlimited tram rides in Kochi City! The bus operates on an hourly or bi-hourly schedule depending on the day, and the friendly drivers can assist you with questions. Inside, the buses are comfortable, with screens displaying stops in Japanese and English. If you plan to visit Katsurahama, be sure to buy the more expensive ticket. This is a convenient and affordable way to explore Kochi's beautiful surroundings.

title: 京都伏見　吟醸酒房「油長（あぶらちょう）」
description: Located in Fushimi, Kyoto, 'Aburachō' is a captivating sake house where you can taste sake from 19 different breweries. The shop offers a selection of 80 types of sake, including ginjo, daiginjo, and junmai, allowing you to savor each unique flavor using special tasting cups. Notably, the deep flavors of 'Kyoto Shukimai 35% polished Izutsuya Denbee' and 'Tamanohikari Denshō Yamahai Junmai Daiginjo' are truly remarkable. Enjoying sake enhances the allure of Kyoto, and the experience of strolling through the sake brewery streets while slightly tipsy in the winter twilight creates lasting memories.

title: Ro to Matagi Restaurant, Sangenjaya
description: While searching for Niku Zushi in Sangenjaya, we stumbled upon Ro to Matagi (炉とマタギ) next door. This unique restaurant specializes in deer meat and is housed in a renovated Showa-era building. The lively izakaya-style first floor contrasts with the quiet, hunting lodge vibe of the second floor. The menu features Ezo deer, Inobuta (a hybrid of wild boar and pig), and Bobo Yasai with Matagi Cauda dip. The deer meat was tender and flavorful, while the Inobuta was equally delicious. A perfect spot for those seeking a new culinary adventure!

title: Yokohama’s Soji
description: The beautiful long corridor 'Hyak-ken-rou-ka' (百間廊下) stretches 152 meters, symbolizing the boundary between the sacred and the ordinary. At 4 AM, a young monk runs through the temple corridors, ringing a loud wake-up bell, marking the start of a new day. Fifteen minutes later, 160 monks begin their morning zazen on meditation platforms. Soji-ji, one of the two largest Zen temples of the Soto sect, was established after a fire destroyed its original buildings, leading to its reconstruction in Yokohama. Located just a 7-minute walk from JR Tsurumi station, this temple is uniquely close to the city. The temple grounds feature twelve large buildings and a cemetery, covering nearly 50,000 square meters. Visitors are welcome to explore the beautiful grounds and can also experience the interiors of the temple buildings.

title: Kawasaki Daishi: A Beautiful and Famous Temple in Kawasaki
description: Kawasaki Daishi (川崎大師) is one of the must-visit temples during your stay in Japan. With easy access and a vibrant local atmosphere, this temple is grand and beautiful. It attracts a mix of locals, tourists, and special visitors. Each year, nearly 3 million people visit for Hatsumode on New Year's Eve to offer their prayers. The temple also hosts monthly fairs, Noh theater performances, and a charming wind chime market in July, providing a great opportunity to experience traditional culture. Kawasaki Daishi is known as a center for spreading the teachings of Kobo Daishi. Don't miss the tea ceremony event in April if you're interested in traditional Japanese culture.

title: Vintage Shopping in Hiroshima
description: Hiroshima city center is a haven for shoppers, especially on Hondori, the main shopping arcade. While many stores focus on current fashion trends, vintage lovers will find a special charm in timeless pieces. Initially, I thought Hiroshima lacked vintage shops until I discovered four fantastic stores on the fifth floor of Sunmall: Union Rag, Rag Moo, Yellow, and 3びきの子ねこ (Kitten Miki). These shops offer high-quality vintage clothing and accessories from the 60s to the 90s at reasonable prices. Union Rag and Rag Moo boast the largest and most varied stock, including popular Doc Martens and Converse shoes. Embrace the vintage allure and enjoy creating unique outfits that stand out.

title: Kanazawa Hakkei’s Chiyomoto [Closed]
description: Chiyomoto (千代本) is an authentic Japanese restaurant that frequently appeared in Hiroshige's ukiyo-e woodblock prints around 1834. This restaurant has stood for almost 200 years in the heart of what was once a famous scenic spot—Kanazawa Hakkei. All rooms in Chiyomoto face the sea, and in the past, guests arrived by boat. The interior is purely Japanese, retaining the atmosphere of its glorious past. The dishes are beautifully presented, with fresh ingredients cooked to perfection. Chiyomoto offers a unique experience where history and stunning views come together.

title: Hinano Organic Buffet in Moriya [Closed]
description: Hinano (旬菜食健ひな野) is a buffet-style restaurant that focuses on healthy ingredients, starting in Sendai in 2007. With over 50 outlets nationwide, it offers locally sourced, organic dishes at affordable prices. For ¥1,575 at lunch and ¥2,100 at dinner, you can enjoy a variety of traditional Japanese dishes, including salads, soups, curries, tempura, and tofu. While predominantly vegetarian, there are also meat and fish options available, with seasonal menus that change regularly. Hinano is a great place to indulge in delicious and healthy cuisine, making it a must-visit.

title: A unique pearl jewelry experience at Pearl Miki Discover and learn pearl culture in Iseshima
description:
■Activity details■
Shima, Mie is the birthplace of pearl cultivation. Thanks to abundant ocean resources and time-honored techniques, Shima pearls are known as being some of the highest quality around the world. This program offers participants the chance to visit a pearl farm to learn about the cultivation techniques in person while talking with artisans. They'll also have the chance to collect pearls from oysters and the very rare chance to seed oysters, learning just how difficult the process of pearl cultivation truly is. Finally, participants will use the pearls they collect to make a one-of-a-kind piece of jewelry.

■コンテンツの概要＆ストーリー■
真珠養殖の発祥の地である三重県志摩市。豊かな海と技術が受け継がれる志摩で作られる真珠の品質の高さは世界有数です。本プログラムでは、今もなお稼働している真珠養殖の現場に訪問し、伝統的な養殖手法を間近で見学、職人と直接お話することができます。また、「真珠の取り出し体験」や通常は体験することができない「母貝への核入れ作業」を通して、「真珠づくり」の真の難しさを体感してみてください。そして最後に、取り出した真珠で世界に一つだけのオリジナル真珠ジュエリーを製作しましょう。

#mttakao #chairlift #japan #mttakoadventures #steepestslopeinjapan #mttakaochairlift #japanadventures #mybestjapanmoments #visitjapanjp #viaggiatotravelservices

Mount Takao (高尾山, Takao-san) is a mountain in the city of Hachiōji, Tokyo, Japan. It is protected within Meiji no Mori Takao Quasi-National Park.

Standing 599 metres (1,965 ft) tall and located within an hour of downtown Tokyo, it is a popular hiking spot, with eight hiking courses and more than 2.5 million annual visitors. The Tama Forest Science Garden is also located at the mountain's base.

THE CHAIR LIFT RIDE

In addition to the cable car Mt. Takao also has a chair lift that you can ride to the midway point of the mountain!
The ride time is about 12 minutes so why not enjoy an aerial trip through the mountains?

The distance from “Sanroku Station” at the foot of the mountain to “Sanjo Station” in the middle is about 872m, which is shorter than the distance the cable car travels (The cable car travels a total of 1,020m).

title: Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome | Annual Halloween Pumpkin Month | Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse | Halloween Pumpkins
description:
#yumenoshimatropicalgreenhousedome #halloweentheme #pumpkinpatch #YumenoshimaTropicalGreenhouse #HalloweenPumpkins
Today we’re gonna explore the Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome.

The Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome was created to cover this broad theme of “the relationship between tropical plants and our lives.”
Enjoy the exotic scenery created by the wide variety of tropical plants in the large greenhouse. Learn about the plants and the tropics in the Movie Theater, Information Gallery, and Exhibition Hall. Take a full tour of the museum and learn about the relationship between tropical plants and human life without even realizing it.
Guided tours are offered on Saturdays, Sundays, national holidays, and during long vacations. Enjoy a fun tour while learning in detail about the plants in the greenhouse.

"The Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome (夢の島熱帯植物館, Yumenoshima Nettai Shokubutsukan), also sometimes called the Yumenoshima Tropical Plant Dome, is a botanical garden located at 3-2, Yumenoshima, Kōtō, Tokyo, Japan. It is operated by the Tokyo Metropolitan Park Association and open daily except Mondays; an admission fee is charged.

The greenhouse was established in 1988 in Yumenoshima ('Dream Island') Park, a reclaimed landfill and dumping ground in Tokyo Bay. Its three domes currently contain about 1,000 species of tropical and semitropical plants. The A Dome features rain forest with ferns and waterfall, B Dome represents a tropical village, and C Dome contains vegetation of the Ogasawara Islands. There is also a small carnivorous plant room.

The domes' plant collections include palms, orchids, aquatic plants, Pandanus, Hevea brasiliensis, Samanea saman, Barringtonia racemosa, Satakentia liukiuensis, Cyathea lepifera, C. mertensiana, C. spinulosa, and Dicksonia antarctica." -Wikipedia

Yumenoshima Tropical Greenhouse Dome is celebrating their annual Halloween Pumpkin Month from end of September to First of November. You will see their Halloween theme all around the area, inside the museum and on their front lawn or garden are giant pumpkins where you and your kids can play around. Enjoy and shoot lovely Autumn and Halloween photos which will be a great memorabilia for you and your kids! 

10 minute walk from Shin-Kiba Station, which is 10 minutes from Tokyo Station on the Keiyo Line. Also accessible on the Yurakucho Line.

Fees:  Adults 250 yen,
Ages 65 yrs old and older 120 yen, 
Ages 13–15 yrs old 100 yen. 
Under 12 yrs old are FREE!

title: Hiking in Japan - Sacred Peak Mt. Hakkai 八海山 | Adventures in Yukiguni | Minamiuonuma
description:
Climbing Mt. Hakkai (1778 m) of the Echigo Sanzan Mountains.
Using the Hakkaisan Ropeway the hike took about 7 hours round-trip.

Many tourists flock to Snow Country in the winter months to hit the slopes, but many of these snow resort grounds continue to attract visitors seeking outdoor adventures through mountain climbing in the summer as well.

Mt. Hakkai is a famous mountain in Minamiuonuma that boasts a long history of dedicated climbers coming from all across the country.
There are two impressive shrines dedicated to the mountain at each trail-head, and the mountain's delicious spring water and impressive shape are part of the reason its name has become one of Japan's most reputable sake brands: Hakkaisan.
The mountain is very popular for tourists hiking on summer break and its lookout decks offer beautiful views of the varicolored Uonuma Basin in autumn once the leaves begin to change too.
The mountains in this region are said to bless the locals with many gifts and in the green season these are manifested in the landscape's breathtaking scenery.

title: Mt. Io: Untouched Hokkaido/硫黄山
description:
Teshikaga Town: Mt. Io

Stand inches away from the pulse of the earth
With the distinctive smell of sulfur and alpine plants at much lower altitudes than they usually grow, Mt. Io is like a scene from another planet. Mt. Io is located around 3km from Kawayu Hot Springs, and is called Atosa-nupuri (bare mountain) in Ainu. To this day, sulfur plumes rise from various areas of the mountain, with an incredible rumbling sound. Large-scale sulfur mining once took place here, which played a significant role in Teshikaga Town's development.
Parking is free during the winter (late November to early April).
Parking fees apply during summer: ¥200 for a motorcycle, ¥500 for a car, ¥1,000 for a minibus, ¥2,000 for a large bus
*Mt. Io is currently closed to the public for safety reasons, as there is currently a risk of falling rocks.

Untouched Hokkaido
Eastern Hokkaido has a history and geography all of its own. Despite its location in Japan, it is actually on the North American tectonic plate, and as a result it is full of extremely rare plant life. Eastern Hokkaido locals have coexisted for generations with the area's rare wildlife and the nature in the national parks that those animals call home, and as a result there are many natural areas that are untouched by human hands.

title: Samurai -SABURAU- Exhibition in Nishiki ~Return to the Origin~ Starting March 12, 2022!
description:
The Nishiki Town Tourism Association will hold the 'Samurai -SABURAU- Exhibition in Nishiki ~Return to the Origin~' for 31 days from March 12 (Saturday) to April 10 (Sunday), 2022.

' Samurai -SABURAU- ' Project

' Samurai -SABURAU- ' is derived from the word 'samurai.' This project aims to convey the charm of 'samurai' by collaborating traditional culture, including martial arts and weapons, with pop culture, and to pass it on to future generations.

Through manga, anime, and games, we aim to make traditional culture, which is often perceived as highbrow and difficult by young people, children, and foreigners, accessible and enjoyable for everyone.

At the 'Samurai -SABURAU- Exhibition in Nishiki' in March 2022, numerous displays will feature the ancient swordsmanship 'Heihō Taisharyū,' known as the best in the west, passed down in Nishiki Town, Kumamoto Prefecture, as well as manga and anime works themed around 'samurai,' original art, videos, and weapons.

1. Exhibition Name
Samurai -SABURAU- Exhibition in Nishiki ~Return to the Origin~
2. Exhibition Period
March 12, 2022 (Saturday) to April 10, 2022 (Sunday) for 31 days
9:00 AM to 4:00 PM (Admission until 3:30 PM) No closed days
Date and Time
March 12, 2022 (Saturday)
Reception starts at 9:30 AM
Opening ceremony at 10:00 AM

3. Venue
Nishiki Town Historical Museum of the Navy Air Base (Nishiki Secret Base Museum)
(2-107, Kinoshita Nishi, Nishiki Town, Kumamoto Prefecture, 868-0301)
4. Admission Fee
You can view the exhibition by entering the Nishiki Town Historical Museum of the Navy Air Base.
・Adults (high school students and above) 800 yen ・Elementary and junior high school students 500 yen ・Preschool children free

5. Overview
'Heihō Taisharyū,' which has ties to Nishiki Town, is one of Japan's traditional martial arts that has been passed down for over 450 years. We continue activities to convey Heihō Taisharyū and Japanese traditional culture with disciples from both Japan and abroad.
This exhibition has been held in nine locations domestically and internationally since responding to requests for an event in Italy in 2019, and it will be the first homecoming exhibition in Nishiki Town, Kumamoto Prefecture.
The exhibition will feature displays themed around Japan's 'samurai,' demonstrations of Heihō Taisharyū, swords, national treasures from Aso Shrine, and original works related to subculture such as 'Drifters,' 'Armed Girl Machiavellism,' and original merchandise sales.
・Exhibited works (approximately 200 pieces planned)

Heihō Taisharyū (Cultural Heritage of Japan)
About 450 years ago during the Warring States period, the founder, Marume Kurando no suke, developed a sword technique that utilizes both oneself and the opponent through practical experience and research. The word 'Tai' in Taisharyū can correspond to many kanji such as '体' (body), '待' (wait), '対' (confront), and '退' (retreat). It means to discard the use of 'body,' to discard 'waiting,' to discard 'confrontation,' and to discard 'retreat.'
In other words, it is a natural state of being that can move without thinking. It embodies being in harmony with nature. The term 'Taisharyū' carries this meaning.
Heihō Taisharyū, a traditional martial art with ties to Nishiki Town, is led by the 15th generation Uehara Eriko, with its headquarters in Yatsushiro City, Kumamoto Prefecture, having 100 disciples in Japan and 70 overseas, continuing activities to transmit traditional culture to the world. In May 2017, the cultural heritage 'Cultural Heritage of Sagara born from 700 years of conservatism and innovation' was certified as a Japanese heritage, and Heihō Taisharyū is listed as one of the cultural properties.
Heihō Taisharyū is gaining attention as a traditional martial art of Japan overseas. In 2022, a book on Taisharyū is scheduled to be published in the UK, and as part of the publication promotion, over 50 videos centered on Kumamoto's traditional culture are being distributed on YouTube.
Heihō Taisharyū Kenjutsu Dojo Ryūsenkan Official Website https://www.taisharyu.jp/

Since 2014, Heihō Taisharyū has started training seminars with disciples in Europe, with about 500 participants annually. In 2019, at the World Karate Championship held in Venice, Italy, 6,000 people attended the demonstration and exhibition introducing Japanese culture 'Samurai Expo SABURAU in ITALY.'

Domestically, in the same year, a one-night-only (4 hours) 'Samurai Expo SABURAU Homecoming Exhibition' was held at the National Treasure Aso Shrine (Hitoyoshi City, Kumamoto Prefecture), attracting 500 visitors and garnering significant attention.

The Samurai -SABURAU- Exhibition will feature a fusion of traditional martial arts and subculture displays and events. The lineup of subculture works will mainly include 'Drifters,' serialized in Shōnen Gahōsha's 'Monthly Hours,' and 'Armed Girl Machiavellism,' serialized in KADOKAWA's 'Monthly Shōnen Ace.'
The main characters in these popular works are practitioners of Taisharyū, leading to a collaborative effort such as providing original drawings.

Relationship with Nishiki Town
Located in the southern part of Kumamoto Prefecture, Nishiki Town is known for its production of agricultural products such as pears and peaches. In 2018, a museum introducing the 'Hitoyoshi Navy Air Base,' whose history was clarified after 70 years post-war, opened.
The town's catchphrase is 'The Land of Swordmasters and Fruits.'
A kendo tournament honoring the swordmaster 'Marume Kurando no suke' has been held 51 times to date.
Nishiki Town has supported Heihō Taisharyū's overseas activities as part of its promotional efforts. In 2017, Nishiki Town received a letter of appreciation from the mayor of Turin, Italy, for its activities introducing Japanese culture alongside Taisharyū.

title: Hike along the Akan River: Untouched Hokkaido/阿寒川リバーサイドハイク
description:
You’ll be hard-pressed to find a more beautiful hiking spot than this tranquil river surrounded by forest with natural hot springs along the way
The pure waters of the Akan River are home to rainbow trout and whitespotted char. In winter, you can hike on snowshoes through the snow-covered forest by the river. Hot springs can be found along the river, making the perfect end point for your hike. If the timing is right, you might even see wildlife such as foxes, raccoon dogs (tanuki) and Yezo deer, which drink from the hot springs to get minerals.

"Where water kamuy and fire kamuy meet"
The indigenous Ainu people of Hokkaido place great importance on coexisting with nature, where they believe that deities reside. There are two types of deities in nature – the deity of fire (apefuchi-kamuy) and the deity of water (wakkaushi-kamuy). The Akan River is a holy ground where the two meet, and the two types of kamuy are believed to provide the nutrients that the forest wildlife lives on.

title: Kotan no Yu: A free open-air hot spring by Lake Kussharo/Untouched Hokkaido/コタンの湯
description:
This natural open-air hot spring bath will make you feel like you’re bathing in Lake Kussharo itself
This hot spring bath surrounded by stones is just 5m from Lake Kussharo, creating the illusion that you are bathing in Lake Kussharo itself. In winter, the warm water runs into the lake, attracting swans that you can see right before your eyes. As you look out over the lake, you'll feel as if the swans are bathing in the hot spring with you. This vast natural paradise is stunningly beautiful no matter what time of day you visit, with incredible sunsets over the mountains beyond the lake and stars as far as the eye can see at night. Admission is free and free parking is available. Basic men's and women's changing facilities are available. The bath is surrounded by stones. While there is a large stone in the center dividing the bath in two, each side is visible from the other side, so bathing is basically mixed. Swimwear is OK.

title: Early morning tour of Lake Akan in winter: Untouched Hokkaido/冬の阿寒湖早朝散歩
description:
Take an early morning tour through the snowy scenery around Lake Akan
In winter, you can explore a freezing natural environment where it is not uncommon for early morning temperatures to reach -20°C. The winter chill creates magical natural beauty. You can walk across the completely frozen Akan lake to its island in around 10 minutes. You can also see the sunrise over Mt. Oakan and beautiful natural phenomena such as frost flowers, rime and diamond dust. The tour meets at 6:20, early mornings from late January to mid-March.
In summer, this island can only be reached by boat.

title: Fukutsukasa Sake: Untouched Hokkaido / 釧路の地酒 福司酒造
description:
Fukutsukasa is a brewery that has made seishu sake in Kushiro since 1919.
Fukutsukasa is one of Kushiro's best-known brands. Its name is said to come from fuku wo tsukasadoru, an ancient Japanese concept of inviting good fortune. As Kushiro's only sake brewery, Fukutsukasa makes delicious sake that cannot be imitated elsewhere, and is a firm favorite among Kushiro locals. The main ingredient is Hokkaido rice, brewed in groundwater filtered by the great nature of eastern Hokkaido.

title: Narusawa Ice Cave | Mt. Fuji Tour | 鳴沢氷穴 | Narusawa Hyōketsu
description:
#narusawa #narusawaicecave #mtfuji #yamanashi #japanadventures #touristsppotsinjapan #familyadventureinjapan

The Narusawa "Hyoketsu" Ice Cave is located at the east entrance to the Aokigahara Jukai "sea of trees" forest, and is regarded as one of the tourist spots within the Fuji Five Lakes area that can be visited throughout the year.
Over 1150 years ago, during year 6 of the Jogan era (864 a.d.), Nagaoyama, a flank volcano of Mt. Fuji erupted. The red hot lava flow (Aokigahara Maruo) descended between ancient parasitic volcanoes, creating this two-tunnel type cave. After being designated by the Ministry of Education as a natural monument in 1929, it was introduced to the world as a geological wonder.
By the way, the tree-type lava bed is said to have the most spiracles in the world.

Since the cave is situated in a ring-like manner, visitors can view its various features by making one circular loop.

The average temperature inside the cave is 3degC, that's why it is called an Ice Cave. The total length of the cave is 150m and requires 6-7 mins to have a complete view inside the cave.

description:
Artist#sakura #cherryblossoms #tokyo #chidorigafuchiryokudo #japan

This 700m promenade and park on the west side of the Imperial Palace is particularly impressive during cherry blossom season, when the around 250 sakura trees reach their heavy branches out over the Chidorigafuchi moat. Chidorigafuchi Boathouse, around the middle of the park, is where to rent a boat and paddle out over the water.

It is said that Chidorigafuchi was named because it has the shape of "Chidori". It used to be connected to Hanzo Moat, but it was reclaimed for road construction in 1883, and the moat was divided into two.Somei Yoshino cherry trees and wild cherry trees are planted on the banks of Chidorigafuchi and Hanzo moat, and together with the cherry blossoms of Chidorigafuchi Park managed by the 23 wards of the upper part of the bank, it is one of the most famous cherry blossom viewing spots in Tokyo.

title: Fuji Safari Park | 富士サファリパーク
description:
#fujisafaripark #fujizoo 

Fuji Safari Park

At the foot of Mt. Fuji lies this enormous animal park. Divided into 2 major zones, the Safari Zone and Fureai Zone.

Safari Zone is a 50min drive through where you can find 7 zones of different animals from all over the world. Riding on your own car, you cannot open your windows or doors as it could be too dangerous. But there is an option of riding the Jungle Bus where you can feed the animals yourself. These huge animals come to the jungle bus seeking for food, as close as 20cm apart from you, with just steel mesh in between. You can also opt to try their 4WD vehicle and experience the same as the jungle bus, feed the animals as they come near you and wait to be fed.

The Fureai Zone on the other hand is extremely different as you can have a friendly contact with the animals. You can feed them up close, hold them in your arms and caress them as long as you want. Great for kids and animal lovers.

title: Tsugaru Nuri（津軽塗） Brand Movie
description:
Tsugaru nuri, the traditional crafts of Hirosaki city, Aomori prefecture, Japan.

Tsugaru nuri, from over 300 years ago, have been handed down to the present by its long history up to today to the craftsmen’s patience, hard work, and their aesthetic eyes for beauty.

From painting the surface of Cypress tree, and repetition of sharpening and polishing, the solid and elegant lacquer ware is completed after a long process of over forty steps for more than two months. It is also called “Baka nuri” meaning Foolish painting, because of the long careful process.

This movie shows the handworks of craftsmen, and four types of techniques "Kara-nuri", "Nanako-nuri", "Monsha-nuri", and "Nishiki-nuri" with the beauty of the Tsugaru district.

The area of East Hokkaido where you'll find the Kushiro Shitsugen Wetland, Lake Akan and Lake Mashu is a shining jewel of natural beauty. The indigenous Ainu people believe that Kamuy (deity) dwells in everything, and treasure a symbiotic relationship with the waters' natural bounty.
This belief continues to thrive in this historically and geographically unique land, which is home to countless species of wildlife, including the incredibly rare Blakiston's fish owl. Visit in winter to see red-crowned cranes, Steller's sea eagles and white-tailed eagles.
Welcome to Untouched Hokkaido, a land of natural beauty that has been preserved since ancient times.
歴史的・地理的に、ユニークな場所である東北海道は、⽇本でありながら北⽶プレートに位置するため、その植⽣はとてもに珍しい種類で溢れている。この⼟地だからこそ出逢える希少な野⽣⽣物、そして多くの⽣き物が暮らす⽇本の国⽴公園はその⾃然と共⽣する地元の⼈々がずっと昔から守りぬいてきた『⾃然が⼿付かずで残る場所（Untouched
Hokkaido）』。 東北海道、この地域は豊かな清流でつながっており、日本の特別天然記念物でもある、優雅で美しいタンチョウが住んでいる。北海道の先住民族であるアイヌの言葉で、タンチョウはサロルンカムイ（湿原に住む神）と呼ばれていた。

title: Enchanting Tokyo HACHIJOJIMA Island (Full ver.)／八丈島
description:
Hachijojima Island, which is less than an hour’s flight from Tokyo, is an island where you can enjoy the great outdoors.
With one of the highest precipitation rates in Japan, Hachijojima has its own unique environment including giant ferns and potholes carved into the rock by ever-flowing spring water.
On the island, you can enjoy hiking as well as running and fishing.
After enjoying physical activities, visitors can relax in a natural hot spring surrounded by rich nature, making it the perfect environment for a refreshing weekend getaway.

Access
・Airplane (Haneda Airport-Hachijojima Airport) 3 flights/day [approximately 55 minutes, one way]
・Boat (Takeshiba Pier, Tokyo- Hachijojima, Sokodo or Yaene Port): Runs daily [10 hours and 20 minutes, one way]

Hachijojima Tourist Information
https://www.gotokyo.org/en/destinations/izu-and-ogasawara-islands/hachijojima-island/index.html

東京から飛行機で1時間弱で到着する八丈島は、大自然と向き合える島です。
日本でも降水量がトップクラスとなる八丈島は、巨大なシダ植物や、枯れることのない湧水によって岩盤が削られたポットホールなど独自の自然を育んでいます。
島ではトレッキングはもちろんランニングや釣りなども楽しめます。
身体を動かすアクティビティを楽しんだ後は、豊かな自然に囲まれた天然温泉でリラックスすることができ、週末のリフレッシュには最適な環境です。

Aogashima Island, located 358 kilometers (222 miles) south of urban Tokyo in the Pacific Ocean, was the only Japanese location selected as the “World’s Top 13 Most Beautiful Views to See Before you Die” by a US-based NGO, thereby attracting attention from around the world.
The video “Enchanting Tokyo AOGASHIMA Island” introduces the unique landscape of the island, including the world-famous double caldera and geothermic “hingya” steam eruptions.
The video also explores the island’s way of life and beliefs that coexist in harmony with nature.

・Boat (Hachijojima, Sokodo or Yaene Port-Aogashima, Sanpo Port): 4-5 trips weekly [2 hours and 30 minutes, one way]

description:

description:
🎨Second Round of Drawing on the Blackboard🎨

This time, I drew the auspicious Kagura performance "Ebisu (恵比寿)" which can also be written as "恵比須".

The performance depicts the god of prosperous business and abundant fishing, Ebisu, fishing. As bait to catch sea bream, we scatter rice cakes and sweets to the audience. It is said that picking these up as "seeds of fortune" will bring happiness✨️

Ebisu's cheerful expression and light dance are so divine that they brighten the heart when watched.

"Catch a fish, catch a fish, let's catch a sea bream with shrimp♪"
"Scatter, scatter, let's scatter the seeds of fortune♪"

Ebisu is often performed at celebratory occasions🎣

In line with the season, I made it spring-like, combining cherry blossoms and Ebisu🌸. The point is that the scales of the sea bream are represented by cherry blossoms.

I am also accepting requests for drawings on the blackboard! I prefer themes related to Kagura or Kitahiroshima Town.

I hope to create a drawing that will warm the hearts of the customers visiting the tourist information center.
Stay tuned for the next one!!

title: Mysterious 'Ice Waterfall Tour' ⛄⛄ #KitaHiroshimaTown #KitaHiroshimaCity
description:
Have you ever climbed a snowy mountain??⛄️

Limited season! A special project by Mr. Kurata from the wild glamping and camping site 'Ryuzu no Mori' in Toyohira 🧊 Mysterious Ice Waterfall Monitor Tour 🧊 was attended by staff from the tourism association!!

This is my second time climbing Mount Ryuzudake in mid-winter. I advance while firmly stepping on the snow.

To keep the mountain climbing interesting, Mr. Kurata shares mountain trivia and quizzes along the way 🏔️

Just as I started to feel a bit out of breath, we arrived at the first highlight, 'Koma Falls.' If the timing is right, you can see the frozen waterfall in all its glory 🧊. On this day, the weather was a bit nice, causing some melting, but there were still icicles here and there, and the frozen grass and trees looked like jewels 💎.

At the second spot, 'Kuro Falls,' there were icicles that had melted and pierced into the ground!! They were about the same height as our staff member, who is 167 cm tall... you can really feel the power of nature.

And the beauty of the snowy mountain bathed in sunlight is breathtaking!! It was a quiet and mystical space where only the chirping of birds and the sound of the wind could be heard.

After descending, we had lunch at the nearby cafe 'Caf'e de la Richesses 六' 🍽️

Mr. Kurata's special spice keema curry and homemade marmalade tea warmed me right up! Chatting by the fireplace about our impressions of the tour was a leisurely and luxurious time ☺️.

This was a mysterious ice waterfall tour where we could fully enjoy the winter scenery of Mount Ryuzudake, which is not often seen✨.

🧊 This ice waterfall tour will also be held on ★2/8 (Sat) and ★2/11 (Tue)!!! If you're interested, please DM Ryuzu no Mori. (Please note that there is a possibility of the tour taking place in snowy conditions, so beginners in mountain climbing are advised to refrain.) Search for 'Ryuzu no Mori' 🔍

title: Every Day is Yoron 4K Yoron Island, Nature moves on, as do we
description:
Learn more about Yoron Island
https://travel.yorontou.info/

The title "日日是与論＝にちにちこれよろん" is an homage to the Zen phrase "日日是好日 (Be grateful for each day and live as it is)." In 2020, after experiencing the pandemic, we learned that our "daily life" is indeed a precious overlap of "special" moments.

From the perspective of being a tourist island, Yoron Island has certainly suffered significant damage due to the pandemic, but this is true everywhere in the world. Moreover, it is an island that has overcome natural disasters such as annual typhoons and wars.

In this work presented at ART&FACTORY JAPAN, we express the beauty and resilience of the island through the personification of various "lives" that inhabit Yoron Island, while accepting the great cycles of nature that repeat day by day (though, to those living in other cities, daily life in Yoron may seem like a great non-daily experience).

From Yoron Island, we hope to send a message of encouragement to other remote islands and depopulated towns facing similar issues, as well as to all people living in the "now."

開港当時から異文化を受け入れてきた神戸トアロードは、昔からいわゆるダイバーシティの考え方が根付いています。
「風のまち」と呼ぶ人もあり。港町の特性からか、来る人を拒まず、去る人を追わず。
独自のカルチャーが根付き、その独特の磁場に弾き寄せられて、わざわざ遠くから足を運ぶファンの多いまちです。わざわざ、神戸のなかでも、この「南北１kmの美しい寄り道」を選んで歩く人の人生はきっとユニークかつ、豊かなものに変わるでしょう。

title: The Voice of the Scarecrow Village - かかしの村の声 [ #Poem #Tokushima #filmfestival ]
description:
Our first video that is officially selected for a film festival!
https://jwtff.world/aiovg_videos/2022_j201/

The foreigner who visited the sky village where time has stopped quietly leaves the memories of that person who traveled with the welcoming scarecrow in the village. Just to mark that eternal moment.

This poem is meant to reflect our final adventure together and this beautiful Nagoro Scarecrow Village and its surroundings. Making youtube videos together have gotten us to go places we never knew we would. Although it didn't last long, we have been able to see and experience things we never imagined possible in Japan. I visited Iya Valley with my friend last year. We had the time of our life. It was only the two of us. I documented our travel around Shikoku. After our trip to Shikoku, we came back to Tokyo and we went our separate ways. I have never seen her since, and she never had the chance to see this video. With this video, I hope besides promoting the Nagoro “Scarecrow” Village, I can reach her out somehow. The poem represents my feelings towards her after our trip but at the same time, it also symbolizes reaching out to people from far away to see the Nagoro “Scarecrow” Village.

Last year, I visited Iya Valley with my friend. We had a special time there. It was a space just for the two of us. I documented our journey in Shikoku. After returning to Tokyo, we went our separate ways. Since then, I have not seen her, and she never had the chance to see this film. With this film, I hope to not only promote the Nagoro “Scarecrow” Village but also somehow reach out to her. This poem expresses my feelings towards her after our trip. At the same time, it conveys my desire for people from afar to see the Nagoro “Scarecrow” Village.

I would like to promote the Nagoro “Scarecrow” Village in Tokushima Prefecture. When I visited this place with my friend, there were no tourists other than us. The local people we met were very friendly, and their desire for more people to visit their beautiful hometown and its surroundings was palpable. Some of my foreign friends have heard of this place, but very few have actually seen it. Most have never even heard of it. However, after showing them the film, they expressed a desire to visit this place. They also asked about the directions and the costs needed to get there. I hope that after watching this film, they will visit the village in Iya Valley and other places, just like my friend did.

title: ReVIEW! #Hida Takayama Ichinomiya Town
description:
Morio Inako, chairman of the Hida Ichinomiya Tourism Association, will introduce the charms of the town.
Ichinomiya Town is located in the southern part of Takayama City and is an area steeped in history and tradition. Surrounded by beautiful nature, it is a popular area for green tourism, where you can experience farming that takes advantage of the environment and interact with local people. Among them, Hida Ichinomiya Mizunashi Shrine is considered to be the most prestigious shrine in Hida, and is worshiped and revered by the people living in the area. You can also see and experience a variety of other genres, such as the Cabinet Office-certified Doburoku Special Zone, the 1,100-year-old Garyu Cherry Tree, a walk on Mt. Iyama where you can see the watershed, and winter sports.
Please come to Ichinomiya Town.
(About 20 minutes by car from downtown Takayama)

title: ReVIEW! #Hida Takayama Takane Town
description:
Mamoru Kosaka, chairman of the Hida Takane Tourism Association, will introduce the charms of the town.
Takane Town is located in the southeast of Takayama City, on a highland surrounded by nature overlooking Mt. Norikura and Mt. Ontake. Because it is adjacent to the Kiso region of Nagano Prefecture, its history, culture, and customs are strongly influenced by Kiso, and it is known as a foreign place even within Hida. Takane Town is also famous for being a production area for Kiso horses, and the stone Buddha statues made for memorial services for horses are filled with stories between people and horses. Takane Town is putting a lot of effort into fermented foods, and its whiskey distillery, which was repurposed from an abandoned school, is attracting a lot of attention. In addition, suna, which is pickled with lactic acid bacteria without using any salt, and country miso, which is often used in Hida's local cuisine, are also actively produced. The region's unique cool summers and cold winters are conducive to growing these fermented foods. It is also a unique place with many other attractions such as Hibata Soba, Takane Corn, Nomai Pass, and Mt. Ontake.
Please come to Takane Town.
(Approximately 50 minutes by car from Takayama city center)

"Kumano is a feeling - not a form - a manifestation of the Divine Intangibles, a celebration of life's powerful vitality.
It is a peaceful place in nature to take a moment to reflect on, and reaffirm one's future direction and meaning of life - a sacred space to open one's mind, heart, soul; all of one's senses; and let the artificial boundaries and borders of the modern world disappear - allowing us to contemplate life as one unified humanity on planet earth.
The importance of a pilgrimage to Kumano is not in its completion, but rather what you take home after internalizing your experience" (Kumano Kodo, 2019).

Kumano is the abode of the Gods.
The complicated landscape is considered a sacred site of healing and salvation for a diversity of faiths, and is a symbolic example of Japan's syncretic religious traditions.

Mihama Town is in Mie prefecture, Japan.

There are many outstanding nature and life which you would understand what Japanese people are really.

【Gojō Ryōchi (Abbot) × Kimpusenji】
Shugendo, a path to enlightenment through rigorous training in the deep mountains, is an ancient mountain faith in Japan. Kimpusenji, located on the slopes of Yoshino Mountain in the Kii Mountain Range, is a center of Shugendo established by En no Gyoja in the 7th century, preserving many tangible cultural assets. One of the important tasks of Abbot Gojō Ryōchi is to protect cultural heritage such as the principal deity Zōō Gongen, ensuring that they can be passed down in the future.

Tokushima is located on the eastern side of Shikoku, and it has the highest number of preserved rural stages in Japan. This outdoor stage was built by local residents in the late Edo period to express gratitude for a bountiful harvest. The Awa Puppet Theater, which has always been loved by local residents, is performed on this stage. This is a representative traditional art form that has been passed down through the ages.

title: I visited the national scenic spot and natural monument 'Oni no K城' (Kumano City) | Tourism Mie | Mie Prefecture Travel Information
description:
I visited Oni no K城 in Kumano City. This time, I walked to the Oku no Kido. (Photo taken on 2019.4.10)

It is a natural art created by uplift, weathering, and wave erosion, stretching endlessly for 1 km facing the Kumano Sea, designated as a national scenic spot and natural monument. At the summit, there are the ruins of a castle from the Sengoku period, and a hiking course is developed that connects to the Kumano Kodo and Matsumoto Pass. From the observation deck known as Oni no Mihara, you can get a panoramic view of the Kumano Sea.

The hiking course leading to the summit is lined with cherry blossoms, and in spring, four types of cherry blossoms bloom one after another, delighting the eyes of tourists who visit for an extended period.

title: FARM STAY in JAPAN! - Traditional Japanese travel experience in Akita
description:
What better way is there to experience Japanese culture than being invited into a local farmer's home to hang out and stay the night? On our recent trip to Akita (秋田県), we did a farm homestay in the humble town of Odate (大館市). We stayed with Yamauchi-san and his wife and together we cooked the local cuisine - Kiritanpo (切りたんぽ).

Kiritanpo is essentially mashed rice, cooked on a stick over an open fire, and then either eaten with a delicious miso glaze, or put in another meal, such as a hotpot - perfect for a chilly winter night! We had a quick trip to an onsen, and afterwards we stayed up late into the night having drinks, laughing and enjoying each other's company.

The next day Yamauchi gave us a personal tour of his town, giving us all the insider knowledge that you couldn't discover by yourself as a tourist. We even got to see and pet the famous Akita Inu's (秋田犬)! Even with our limited Japanese speaking ability, Yamauchi-san and his wife were incredibly accommodating and we can't thank them enough for such a fun experience.

title: Japan Heritage Tourism (Higashiomi Edition) - Visiting Eigenji, a Culture of Water and Life
description:
【🍁Japan Heritage & Water Heritage 'Eigenji'⛩】
'Eigenji' (永源寺), located in Higashiomi City, Shiga Prefecture, is the head temple of the Rinzai sect Eigenji branch, boasting a history of over 650 years.

The temple grounds feature a main hall (Hōjō) with a thatched roof made of reed, one of the largest in the country, as well as designated tangible cultural properties of the prefecture.

Nestled in deep nature, the temple complex offers a picturesque view throughout the seasons, and the vibrant red autumn leaves 🍁 that blanket the grounds attract many visitors from across the country, making it one of the top spots for autumn foliage in the Kansai region.

While certain areas are usually off-limits to the public, special tours can be arranged with volunteer guides. Enjoy the charm of Eigenji, where the autumn leaves beautifully contrast with the ancient temple, through our video.

description:
This work is an award-winning entry in the video contest conducted by Fukui Prefecture, themed "Subtly Amazing, Fukui." 
【Comment from the Video Creators】 
We are a video production company called Seven D, based in Fukui City, operated by Takashima and Imajo. Since 2016, we have been uploading videos themed around the ordinary landscapes of Fukui on our YouTube channel. In creating this video, we contemplated what it means to be subtly amazing and what makes Fukui wonderful. We believe the beauty of Fukui lies in its scenery and landscapes. The abundant nature brought by rich water possesses a grandeur that remains constant even amidst the changing tides of time. This beauty is not only found in well-known tourist spots and landmarks but also overflows in the most ordinary places. The scenery reflects the number of people living in Fukui, those who visit, and those who think of Fukui. In the video, we weave together not only the tourist spots you know but also the wonderful landscapes and nature we have discovered, creating a story that encourages viewers to come to Fukui and find their own special scenery. The title expresses our desire for you to cut through the obscured views of Fukui's landscapes in the sea of clouds and to bring your perspective into the unseen world (Fukui). The video is in 4K. We struggled to recreate the beauty of Fukui. Thank you for your support.

title: Sea of Clouds Over Lake Mashu in the Early Morning / 摩周湖早朝雲海
description:
Website: http://untouchedhokkaido.jp/
FACEBOOK: https://www.facebook.com/untouchedhokkaido/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/untouched_hokkaido/?hl=en

Around 20 minutes by car from Kawayu Hot Springs is Lake Mashu Viewpoint No. 3. Arrive here between sunrise and around 8:00 AM and you might see an incredible sea of clouds. The clouds covering the sky change from one movement to the next - you won't be able to tear your eyes away! The scene is completed by waves of clouds that flow over Lake Mashu from the surrounding mountains. June to September is the best time to see the sea of clouds in Teshikaga Town. Lake Mashu Viewpoint No. 3 is the best vantage point, at over 100m higher than Viewpoint No. 1. If you're lucky, you'll see a "double sea of clouds" around you, with clouds covering both Lake Mashu and Lake Kussharo! Make sure you check the best time of morning and viewing conditions in advance, as it changes depending on the season and the weather.

川湯温泉から摩周第３展望台までは車で約20分。日の出前から朝8時ぐらいまでが雲海の見頃だ。空を覆う雲海は、刻一刻と姿を変え、見る者の心を奪う。雲の波が外輪山から摩周湖に流れ込むように湖面を覆う、その様は圧巻の一言。弟子屈町で雲海を見るなら6月から9月がベストシーズン。摩周第3展望台の標高は、第1展望台よりも100メートル以上高く、雲海スポットとしては第３展望台がおすすめ。運が良ければ、360度見渡す限り雲海に埋め尽くされた摩周湖と、屈斜路湖両方の雲海、通称「ダブル雲海」を見ることができる！ 雲海の見ごろの時間帯は、季節や気象条件などにより異なるので事前の確認を。

title: Kagami no Ma Cruise in the Headwaters of the Kushiro River / 釧路川源流クルーズ・鏡の間
description:
Website: http://untouchedhokkaido.jp/
FACEBOOK: https://www.facebook.com/untouchedhokkaido/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/untouched_hokkaido/?hl=en

The Kushiro River is the only river that flows out of Lake Kussharo. It runs through Kushiro Shitsugen Wetland and out to sea. A short distance to the side of the Kushiro River is a magical spot called Kagami no Ma. Kagami no Ma is Japanese for "mirror room" and you'll see why as soon as you see how clear this spring is. The water remains below 10°C all year round, and the area offers a vastly different scene from the Kushiro River nearby. With its cool air, crystal-clear water and lush greenery, Kagami no Ma will captivate you.

屈斜路湖から流れ出る唯一の川、釧路川。川は釧路湿原へとつながり最後は海へ流れ出る。釧路川から少しだけ脇にはいったところに「鏡の間」と呼ばれる神秘のスポットがある。湧き水から成る「鏡の間」は、その名に相応しく透明度が抜群に高い！水温は四季を通して10度以下で触るとひんやり冷たい。釧路川との違いをしっかり感じることができる。清涼な空気、鏡面の水面、澄んだ緑、訪れる者を魅了する神秘の空間。

title: Canoe Cruise around Wakoto Peninsula / 和琴半島一周カヌークルーズ
description:
Website: http://untouchedhokkaido.jp/
FACEBOOK: https://www.facebook.com/untouchedhokkaido/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/untouched_hokkaido/?hl=en

Wakoto Peninsula is a peninsula that is about 3km around, jutting into a lake with a circumference of 57km. Its name comes from the Ainu phrase "wakkochi", which means "the narrow part of a fish's tail". The peninsula is a fascinating volcanic area, with hot springs everywhere and an area called Oyakotsu Jigoku (Oyakotsu Hell) at the tip of the peninsula, where plumes of smoke rise from the ground. Covered with deep forest, Wakoto Peninsula offers new natural splendor with each season: North Japanese hill cherry blossoms in spring, new greenery in early summer, colorful foliage in autumn. On a sunny day, Lake Kussharo is at its clearest, offering a view that will take your breath away. After you paddle around the peninsula, Mrs. Hiratsuka will serve you a hearty homemade lunch near the stunning Oyakotsu Jigoku. Made with local ingredients from Teshikaga and the surrounding area, every option will have you smacking your lips in satisfaction. The heartfelt hospitality you'll receive will make this the best canoe cruise you've ever been on.

Kazuaki and Ai Hiratsuka
This husband and wife duo are guides at Northeast Canoe Center, Ltd.
After encountering Canadian canoeing in 1986, they decided to recreate the experience on the beautiful Lake Kussharo and Kushiro River, and began working as tour guides to share the spectacular nature of their hometown through exciting canoe tours.
After a leisurely canoe trip with the Hiratsukas where you’re surrounded by the natural marvels of Lake Kussharo and the Kushiro River, you’ll be treated to a hearty homemade lunch made by Ai.

title: Fishing in Lake Akan and the Akan River / 阿寒湖・阿寒川フィッシング
description:
Website: http://untouchedhokkaido.jp/
FACEBOOK: https://www.facebook.com/untouchedhokkaido/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/untouched_hokkaido/?hl=en

Lake Akan is famous for its marimo moss balls and is surrounded by untouched nature. It's also home to an abundance of native trout species, making it a beloved spot for fly fishing and lure fishing enthusiasts. Fishing is banned until April 30 each year to protect the fish population, but the period from May 1 until autumn is an angler's paradise! Even beginners will find it easy to catch rainbow trout, Japanese char, and kokanee in Lake Akan. Be aware that the area from the mouth of the Akan River at Lake Akan to the Yukan Bridge is a catch-and-release area - the first in Hokkaido (designated in 2003). A recreational fishing charge of JPY1,500 per day applies (to be paid in advance).

マリモの生息で有名な阿寒湖には、手つかずの自然の姿がそのまま残る。そして阿寒湖はネイティブトラウトの宝庫で、多くのアングラー（釣り人）のあこがれの地でもあり、フライフィッシングやルアーフィッシングの聖地とも呼ばれる。5月1日の解禁日から秋にかけては、釣り三昧の休日を過ごせるベストシーズン！ニジマス・アメマス・ヒメマス釣りなどは初心者でも手軽に楽しめる。 ちなみに2003年に北海道で初めてキャッチ＆リリース（再放流）を遊漁規則化したことにより、阿寒川湖流出口から雄観橋下流端はキャッチ＆リリースエリアに設定されている。遊漁料1日.1,500円が必要（事前支払い）。

title: Chikurouen Flagship Store / 竹老園東家総本店
description:
Website: http://untouchedhokkaido.jp/
FACEBOOK: https://www.facebook.com/untouchedhok...
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/untouched_h...

Chikurouen's flagship store is one of the oldest soba noodle restaurants in Hokkaido. With a history of over 140 years, this specialist restaurant has honed its skills and is still striving to improve on its authentic local noodles. Kushiro soba noodles stand out from the rest - they're green! That's because they're made from new buckwheat. The founder of Chikurouen is said to have wanted every customer to enjoy soba noodles made from new buckwheat, and that tradition is still alive today.

Considered one of the oldest soba restaurants in Hokkaido, Chikurouen has been dedicated to soba since its establishment over 140 years ago in the Meiji era. With skills refined over the years, they continue to pursue the authentic taste. The characteristic of Kushiro soba is its green color, which comes from being made with new buckwheat. There are various theories about why the soba is green, but it is said to have been served this way so that customers could always feel like they are enjoying fresh buckwheat. The founder's intention from the beginning is still passed down today.

〒085-0824
3-19 Kashiwagi-cho, Kushiro City, Hokkaido
Tel. 0154-41-6291
http://chikurouen.com/

Historically and geographically, Eastern Hokkaido is a unique place, located on the North American Plate despite being in Japan, resulting in a rich variety of rare plant species. This land is home to rare wildlife that can only be encountered here, and the national parks of Japan, where many creatures live, have been preserved by the local people who have coexisted with nature for a long time, known as 'Untouched Hokkaido.' Eastern Hokkaido is connected by rich clear streams, and is home to the elegant and beautiful Tancho, a special natural monument of Japan. In the language of the Ainu, the indigenous people of Hokkaido, the Tancho is called Sarorunkamuy (the god that lives in the marsh). Water nurtures life while magically transforming into various forms.

title: Sanin(mountain’s yin) Coast
description:
In the Chugoku region of Japan, the north of the Chugoku Mountains has been called Sanin(mountain’s yin) and the south has been called Sanyo(mountain’s yang) for a long time.

When naming a place, it is based on the idea of ​​ancient China that the north and south of the mountain are represented by yin and yang, and the north and south of the river are represented by yang and yin.

This is because in the northern hemisphere, where the sun rises in the southern sky, the north of the mountain is in the shadow and the south is in the sun.

In the case of rivers, there are lands in China that are described as Yinyang in the north and south of the river, such as Rakuyo (the area north of the river called Luoyang) and Huaiyin (south of the river called Huai’an).

In the case of rivers, the light from the south bounces off the surface of the river, illuminating the north of the river, and objects in the south cast shadows on the surface of the river.

The coast of the San'in(mountain’s yin) region on the north side of the Chugoku Mountains faces the Sea of ​​Japan.
Enjoy the scenic landscape of the San'in coast formed by the rough waves of the Sea of ​​Japan generated by the wind blowing from the continent.

title: Trip to Nanto City, Toyama Prefecture - Fukuno Yotaka Festival ~Pre-Festival~
description:
Fukuno Yotaka Festival (福野夜高祭り)
The pre-festival is held every year on April 30th. It takes place at the JR Fukuno Station front square (rotary). The highlight is the Bunkyu large lantern, which stands about 15 meters tall, more than twice the size of the large lanterns that are still passed down in the Fukuno area of Nanto City. It recreates the scale of lanterns made in an era without utility poles.
During the evening festival starting on May 1st, the Yotaka lanterns are paraded around, accompanied by the resonant sounds of the Yotaka drums and the spirited shouts of the young men. The main attraction is the tug-of-war (kenka) that begins around 11 PM on the 2nd. With the lively sounds of clappers, the young men clash against each other's lanterns. The intensity of this tug-of-war captivates the audience with its powerful display. During the main festival, the four town floats visit the Shinmei Shrine, and the portable shrine parades through the town.

title: KOKIRIKO -The Ancient Japanese Folk Song- ｜こきりこ　English Ver.
description:
In Gokayama, a life in harmony with nature has been passed down through generations.
Along with the World Cultural Heritage Gassho-style Village, Kokiriko—believed to be Japan’s oldest folk song—has been faithfully preserved by the locals.
Passed down through generations in the Gokayama region, Kokiriko is a simple folk song and dance with roots in a performing art called Dengaku, which originated around 1,400 years ago during the Taika Reforms. Believed to be the oldest folk song in Japan, its name appears in many ancient documents.

title: Steepest Slope in Japan | Mount Takao Cable Car Ride | Autumn Colors | 高尾山　Takaosan
description:
#mttakao #高尾山 #steepestslopeinjapan #japan #cablecar #autumn #fallfoliage #takaosan #nocopyright #relaxingmusic #slope #fall  #autuminjapan #秋 #秋葉原 #紅葉 #mttakaocablecar

Today we are gonna show you the steepest slope in Japan, the Mt. Takao. Join us as we descend from the mountain top to its base riding a cable car, showing the autumn view of the beautiful and vibrant trees around. Get relaxed with this 6-min trip and get amazed with this nature's wonders.

Mount Takao (高尾山, Takao-san) is a mountain in the city of Hachiōji, Tokyo, Japan. It is protected within Meiji no Mori Takao Quasi-National Park.

Standing 599 metres (1,965 ft) tall and located within an hour of downtown Tokyo, it is a popular hiking spot, with eight hiking courses and more than 2.5 million annual visitors. The Tama Forest Science Garden is also located at the mountain's base.

Mount Takao is closely associated with the Shinto-Buddhist tengu, minor kami from Japanese folklore, and the daitengu Naigubu. The mountain is also renowned for Shugendō, the mountain asceticism focusing on strict discipline. A Buddhist temple, Takaosan Yakuōin Yūkiji, is located on the mountain, and attracts many visitors who pray to the tengu for good fortune. The temple belongs to the Shingon Buddhist sect.

#shinobazupond #shinobazunoike #uenopark #autumn #boatride #boatpond #japan #tokyo ＃不忍池　＃上野公園

Come and join us as we show you the relaxing view of autumn at Shinobazu Pond.

Shinobazu no Ike which is found within the Ueno Park in Taito Ku Tokyo, is historically prominent and usually appears in Japanese history and works of art.

If you wanna ride a boat on the boat pond, make sure to wear a mask, sanitize your hands and let the staff check your temperature. Ticket machine is available at the entrance.

The price of boat ride varies with the type of boat you wanna ride on to. A Cycle boat costs 700 yen, maximum of 2 adults for 30 mins. Swan boat costs 800 yen maximum 3 adults for 30 mins. While a row boat costs 500 yen maximum of 3 adults for 30 mins.

Situated in the south of Ueno Park, the pond is divided in three sections. The Lotus Pond (蓮の池, Hasu no Ike), the Boat Pond (ボートの池, Bōto no Ike) and the third called Cormorant Pond (鵜の池, U no Ike).

The pond has a circumference of about 2 km and a surface area of about 1,100,000 sq meters. It hosts several dozens of types of migratory and stationary birds, whose number at times is over ten thousand. Among them particularly numerous are tufted ducks, pochard, and northern pintails. The pond also contains numerous species of fish, and the lotuses of Lotus Pond, which are grown fully in summer, cover the entire surface of the water, hiding it almost completely.

title: Autumn at Ueno Park Tokyo | 上野公園
description:
#travelvlog #uenopark #uenotokyo #tokyojapan #autumnatuenopark

hey guys welcome to Ueno Park in Tokyo!

Ueno Park (上野公園, Ueno Kōen) is a large public park next to Ueno Station in central Tokyo. The park grounds were originally part of Kaneiji Temple, which used to be one of the city's largest and wealthiest temples and a family temple of the ruling Tokugawa clan during the Edo Period. Kaneiji stood in the northeast of the capital to protect the city from evil, much like Enryakuji Temple in Kyoto.

During the Boshin Civil War, which followed the Meiji Restoration in 1868, Kaneiji suffered nearly complete destruction in a battle between the victorious forces of the new Meiji government and loyalists of the overthrown shogunate. After the battle, the temple grounds were converted into one of Japan's first Western style parks and opened to the public in 1873. A statue of Saigo Takamori, one of the generals in the Battle of Ueno, stands near the park's southern entrance.

At the southwestern end of the park lies Shinobazu Pond, one of many reminders of Kaneiji Temple's former grandeur. The pond represents Lake Biwako (in a reference to Kaneiji's model, the Enryakuji Temple of Kyoto, which overlooks Lake Biwako). On an island in the middle of the pond stands Bentendo, a temple hall dedicated to the goddess of Benten.

Today Ueno Park is famous for the many museums found on its grounds, especially the Tokyo National Museum, the National Museum for Western Art, the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum and the National Science Museum. It is also home to Ueno Zoo, Japan's first zoological garden.

Additionally, Ueno Park is one of Tokyo's most popular and lively cherry blossom spots with more than 1000 cherry trees lining its central pathway. The cherry blossoms are usually in bloom during late March and early April and attract large numbers of hanami (cherry blossom viewing) parties.

Shiraito Falls (白糸の滝, Shiraito no taki) is a waterfall in Fujinomiya, Shizuoka Prefecture, near Mount Fuji, Japan. It is part of Fuji-Hakone-Izu National Park and has been protected since 1936 as a Japanese Natural Monument.[1]

The falls were regarded as sacred under the Fuji cult. Another waterfall, the Otodome Falls is approximately a five-minute walk away.

The Shiraito Falls is listed as one of "Japan’s Top 100 Waterfalls", in a listing published by the Japanese Ministry of the Environment in 1990. It was also selected by the Tokyo Nichi Nichi Shimbun and Osaka Mainichi Shimbun.[2] as one of the 100 Landscapes of Japan in 1927. In 2013 the waterfall was added to the World Heritage List as part of the Fujisan Cultural Site.[3]

Today we are gonna show you the steepest slope in Japan, the Mt. Takao. Join us as we descend from the mountain top to its base riding a cable car, showing the autumn view of the beautiful and vibrant trees around. Get relaxed with this 6-min trip and get amazed with this nature's wonders.

Mount Takao (高尾山, Takao-san) is a mountain in the city of Hachiōji, Tokyo, Japan. It is protected within Meiji no Mori Takao Quasi-National Park.

Standing 599 metres (1,965 ft) tall and located within an hour of downtown Tokyo, it is a popular hiking spot, with eight hiking courses and more than 2.5 million annual visitors. The Tama Forest Science Garden is also located at the mountain's base.

Mount Takao is closely associated with the Shinto-Buddhist tengu, minor kami from Japanese folklore, and the daitengu Naigubu. The mountain is also renowned for Shugendō, the mountain asceticism focusing on strict discipline. A Buddhist temple, Takaosan Yakuōin Yūkiji, is located on the mountain, and attracts many visitors who pray to the tengu for good fortune. The temple belongs to the Shingon Buddhist sect.

title: Tokugawa Nariaki, Mito Komon, and the Low Mountain They Climbed: Recommended Ibaraki Sightseeing
description:
Tenpizan and Otatachibana Hime Shrine (天妃山・弟橘媛神社) located in Isohara Town, Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture.

A low mountain associated with the famous Tokugawa Mitsukuni (Mito Komon) and Tokugawa Nariaki.
If you climb further from the shrine, there is a stone said to be where Mitsukuni sat.
It is said that Ujo Noguchi, known for children's songs like 'Nanatsu no Ko' and 'Shabondama', often climbed Tenpizan to gaze at the scenery when he struggled with his lyrics.
When asked for his address, Ujo would reply, 'My address is Isohara Coast!' indicating his affection for Isohara Coast and Tenpizan.

When you visit Kitaibaraki City, be sure to enjoy the scenery of Isohara Coast that both of them loved!

■ Access

【By Car】10 minutes from the Kitaibaraki IC on the Joban Expressway
【By Train】5 minutes by car or 15 minutes on foot from JR Joban Line 'Isohara Station'

title: ReVIEW!#Hida Takayama Kokufu Town
description:
Mr. Iemitsu Kitamura, chairman of the Kokufu Tourism Association, will introduce the charms of the town.
Kokufu Town is located in the northern part of Takayama City and is an area rich in history and nature. It has been a prosperous area since ancient times, with many cultural assets that can be seen, suggesting that it was the site of the Kokufu, the political center of Hidanokuni, over a thousand years ago. In this town, you can see many cultural assets and historical buildings, including many ancient tombs and excavated items from the Stone Age, as well as the Ankoku-ji Kyozo (national treasure) and the Enku Buddha handed down at Seiho-ji Temple, and is designated as a "Japanese Heritage Site." It also includes the cultural assets that make up the area. Through these things, you will feel a sense of nostalgia and warmth. It is also surrounded by beautiful mountains, allowing you to enjoy the scenery of each season. Especially in spring, the cherry blossoms in Sakurano Park are in full bloom, and the roads along the mountain village are dyed pink with peach blossoms, creating a beautiful scenery. This scenery is known as "Peach Road" and is loved by locals. Furthermore, there are many waterfalls dotted around the Utsue Shijuhachi Falls, which have a water source at an altitude of 1,200m, and you can enjoy trekking and picnicking among the clear streams and forests. Your time here will soothe your soul.
Please come to Kokufu Town.
(About 20 minutes by car from downtown Takayama)

title: TOKYO AKASAKA HIKAWA Shrine
description:
Akasaka Hikawa Shrine, which counts a thousand years since its enshrined.

Deity
: Susano-no-mikoto, Kushinadahime-no-mikoto, Okuninushi-no-mikoto

In the past, Kushinadahime-no-mikoto was rescued by Susano-no-mikoto from the sacrifice of Yamata-no-Orochi, and later became the wife of Susano-no-mikoto. Okuninushi is the descendant of couple, and is also the main deity of Izumo Taisha as a national creation god.

It is said to have originated from Hikawa in Izumo Province, which was the stage for exterminating Yamata-no-Orochi. It begins when a monk who was traveling to Togoku in 951, in his dream, responded to the announcement from the deity when he spent the night at the present Akasaka 4th street and worshiped here.

After that, the shrine built by Yoshimune Tokugawa, the eighth shogun of the Edo Shogunate, escaped the former earthquake and war damage, and conveys the remnants of the time when it was built to the torii gate, guardian dog, and lantern.

Kaneyama Town 100th Anniversary Commemorative Video

－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－－

Kaneyama Town, Yamagata Prefecture, marked the 100th anniversary of its town administration on January 1, 2025.

Over these hundred years, some things were born and some were lost; some remain unchanged, while others continue to shift with each passing moment.

What kind of hundred years have the mountains, the forests, and the clear, flowing rivers witnessed?
Have the mythical creatures of this land watched over this century?
Standing where people reflect on Kaneyama’s hundred years, what winds do they feel, and what skies do they see?

In the autumn of 2024, we held the “Centennial Festival” to celebrate Kaneyama’s hundred years.

Leading up to that day, we traced Kaneyama’s four seasons and its changing townscape, explored the work and history of forestry and other local industries, and encountered the lives and words of the people connected to this town.

Join us as we look back with gratitude and forward with hope—carrying the light of a hundred years into the years to come.

title: Movie 'urar suye' Full Version
description:
A short film 'urar suye' (ウララ スエ) that allows you to experience the Ainu worldview alive in modern times, set in the Ainu Kotan of Lake Akan in Hokkaido, is now available.

【Story】
Yukari (xiangyu), who is active in music in Tokyo, was troubled and unable to fully believe in her potential as an artist. In the midst of this, Yukari is invited by her university classmate, dancer Saya, to visit the Ainu Kotan at Lake Akan in Kushiro (where 'Kotan' means 'village' in the Ainu language).

The Ainu Kotan is also known as the 'City of Creators,' where traditional wood carving, embroidery, songs, and dances are alive in people's daily lives. Furthermore, in the Ainu worldview, it is believed that 'Kamuy' resides in natural objects such as mountains, rivers, animals, and trees, as well as in natural phenomena like fire and thunder, and in tools. As Yukari explores the Ainu Kotan, she re-evaluates her connection to herself and the world by fully experiencing the presence of Kamuy in the daily lives of the people.
